![bug · medium](https://img.shields.io/badge/bug-medium-orange)
`GateModel.restore()` accepts any structured clone of the checkpoint object and only re-runs `assertInvariant()`. A truncated or mixed-version checkpoint can still deserialize into an object that satisfies the current invariants accidentally, while semantically wrong fields like `epoch`, `fault`, or `readPosition` are not versioned. Adding an explicit checkpoint schema/version and validating required fields before `Object.assign` would make restore failures deterministic instead of relying on post-hoc invariant checks.

**Suggestion:**
```suggestion
checkpoint() { return structuredClone({ schema: 'calcify-e2-gate-checkpoint-v1', ...this }); }
  static restore(cut) {
    if (!cut || cut.schema !== 'calcify-e2-gate-checkpoint-v1') throw new Error('CHECKPOINT_SCHEMA');
    const g = Object.assign(Object.create(GateModel.prototype), structuredClone(cut));
    g.windows = Object.assign(Object.create(null), g.windows);
    g.assertInvariant();
    return g;
  }
```

![bug · medium](https://img.shields.io/badge/bug-medium-orange)
`cpuEquivalentCores` and `touchedKeysPerTrade` can evaluate to `Infinity`/`NaN` when a measurement carries inconsistent counters (for example `durationMs === 0` in `deadline`/`final`-adjacent artifacts, or `final.decided === 0`). Since these values are surfaced in the returned assessment, they should be guarded or omitted unless the denominators are known valid to avoid publishing misleading capacity metrics.

**Suggestion:**
```suggestion
cpuEquivalentCores: m.resources && positive(durationMs) ? m.resources.processCpuMs / durationMs : null,
    touchedKeysPerTrade: m.resources && positive(m.final?.decided) ? m.resources.touchedKeys / m.final.decided : null,
```

![bug · high](https://img.shields.io/badge/bug-high-red)
`mkdir(out)` will fail if the caller reuses an existing run directory, and the fixed lock path under `/private/tmp` makes concurrent runs across CI jobs or local shells contend for the same file. That can cause spurious failures or, worse, one invocation unlinking another invocation's lock. Consider using a per-run unique lock file and creating the output directory with `recursive: true` plus an explicit existence check if overwrites should be rejected.

**Suggestion:**
```suggestion
const lockPath = path.join(out, '.reef-financial-rate-capacity.lock');
  const lock = await open(lockPath, 'wx'); // Refuse concurrent capacity loads; no stale-lock auto deletion.
```
